A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FA study. The methods, equations, four figures, ten tables, and Appendices A–B are available and can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original FA experiments on OOD detection and ID classification, together with ablations and sensitivity results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and appendix evaluations.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the same frozen original prompt, trainable forced prompt, shared context vectors, forced-coefficient loss, and MCM/GL-MCM inference procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate ImageNet-1k and eight additional ID datasets against the same conventional and challenging OOD datasets. Appendix coverage is unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments, including the post-hoc, zero-shot, and prompt-learning comparisons. Table 9 revises IDLike scores without adding or removing a comparator.

E3.justification: The ViT-B/16 backbone, few-shot settings, training budgets, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Appendix A's revised wording describes the already present 1-shot and 4-shot results rather than a new protocol.

E4.justification: Tables 5–7 retain the same loss, prompt-initialization, and shared-vector ablations. Figure 4 retains the same K=1–6 sensitivity analysis and plotted trends.

E5.justification: Both specify four trials and report means and standard deviations. Changed standard-deviation values in Table 9 accompany revised results; the uncertainty-reporting practice and stated run count do not change.

E6.justification: Appendix A, Table 9 revises the 1-shot IDLike row: NINCO FPR95/AUROC changes from 79.45/71.59 to 71.61/76.02, and ImageNet-O from 68.80/77.24 to 79.45/71.59. The averages change from 65.24/79.46 to 66.18/79.05, with corresponding standard-deviation updates. FA's results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(7) are unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: exploiting ID knowledge through forced prompt learning, avoiding external auxiliary data, retaining CoOp's trainable-parameter count, and improving OOD detection.

C2.justification: The explanations involving richer ID semantics, SUN contamination, shared-vector benefits in limited-data settings, and saturation with increasing K remain unchanged. No new applicability boundary or limitation is introduced.

D1.justification: Both disclose the same initialization, optimizer, learning rate, batch size, training epochs, temperatures, coefficient K, Nvidia A30 hardware, and code link. No implementation or access information is added.

R1.justification: The same 55 references and related-work positioning are retained. Changed citation back-reference page numbers reflect text reflow rather than different cited works.

P1.justification: v3 shortens affiliations and makes limited grammatical and capitalization edits. Appendix A changes its summary from '4-shot setting' to 'other few-shot settings'; the section organization and substantive narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The figures receive small typography, spacing, and sizing adjustments, particularly the framework labels and plots in Figures 3–4. Page-number footers disappear, while the same figures, captions, and table structures remain substantially intact.

improvement.justification: Appendix A's revised summary better matches its existing 1-shot and 4-shot results, and small figure refinements improve presentation. This is a limited clarity gain. The unexplained IDLike numerical revision does not establish improved FA performance or stronger validation; the scientific contribution and supporting evidence remain essentially unchanged.
